title: Finitely many sections of $\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}$ lie in one $E_X$
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme and $V\in X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ quasi-compact.

1. For a filtered diagram of sheaves of sets (or abelian groups) $(\mathcal F_\alpha)$ on
   $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$, the natural map $\varinjlim_\alpha\mathcal F_\alpha(V)\to(\varinjlim_\alpha\mathcal F_\alpha)(V)$
   is bijective.
2. Consequently $\QbarX(V)=\bigcup_EE_X(V)$, the union over finite subextensions
   $E\subseteq\Qlb$ (the maps $E_X(V)\to\QbarX(V)$ being injective), and any finite set of
   elements of $\QbarX(V)$, or of matrices over it, lies in $E_X(V)$ for a single finite $E$.

proof.text:
(1) Let $\mathcal P$ be the presheaf colimit $U\mapsto\varinjlim_\alpha\mathcal F_\alpha(U)$. We
claim that on quasi-compact objects $\mathcal P$ already satisfies the sheaf condition and
agrees with its sheafification. Every covering of a quasi-compact $W$ in $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$
admits a finite subcovering by quasi-compact (affine) objects (\stacks{0988}), and the fibre
products of these are again quasi-compact when computed over affines. For a finite covering
$\{W_k\to W\}$, the sheaf condition is the equalizer
$\mathcal F(W)\to\prod_k\mathcal F(W_k)\rightrightarrows\prod_{k,k'}\mathcal F(W_k\times_WW_{k'})$,
a finite limit; filtered colimits of sets commute with finite limits, so $\mathcal P$
satisfies it for such coverings. Since the quasi-compact objects form a basis of the site
whose coverings are refined by finite ones, the sheafification of $\mathcal P$ agrees with
$\mathcal P$ on quasi-compact objects. (This is the degree-zero case of \stacks{0739}.)

(2) By [sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x], $\QbarX=\varinjlim_EE_X$, a filtered colimit, so by (1)
$\QbarX(V)=\varinjlim_EE_X(V)$. The transition maps are injective: $E_X\to F_X$ is the
inclusion of a direct summand of a finite free module (a basis of $F$ over $E$ containing
$1$), so injective on sections. Hence the colimit is the union, and finitely many elements
lie in a common $E_X(V)$ because the poset of finite subextensions is filtered.
